key_insight: In disordered perovskite nanocrystal solids, exciton transport is controlled more by energetic disorder than by structural size/shape disorder.
engineering_relevance: Ligand engineering can tune nanocrystal disorder and exciton mobility, directly impacting the performance of LEDs, lasers, and solar cells built from colloidal perovskite films.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy
Compared disorder effects across different alkylamine ligand lengths
Linked polydispersity and quantum confinement to transport efficiency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that longer alkyl-chain ligands produced more monodisperse but smaller nanocrystals with higher energetic disorder, and these solids showed less efficient exciton transport.
watch_item: Improving size uniformity alone may not boost device performance if ligand-induced energetic disorder remains high.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
